0.long_answer: Traumatic neuroma is a benign proliferation of nerve tissue that develops as a reactive hyperplasia following nerve injury or surgical trauma. It is most commonly found near the mental foramen in the oral cavity, where damage to the mental nerve during dental procedures or other surgeries can lead to this lesion. Despite being termed a 'neuroma,' it is not a true neoplasm but rather an irregular arrangement of proliferating nerve fibers and connective tissue resulting from the healing process following trauma.
